summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, end-stage renal disease with two kidney transplants, chronic rejection, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and complex sleep apnea was admitted for new-onset right lower quadrant abdominal pain. Imaging and labs showed no acute pathology; pain was likely due to musculoskeletal or functional causes such as urinary retention and constipation. His tacrolimus dose was adjusted to 6mg twice daily, and insulin was reduced due to hypoglycemia. He remained stable, pain resolved, and was discharged home with plans to follow up on tacrolimus levels, obtain a renal MRI for a growing native kidney cyst, repeat sleep study, and manage bowel and bladder symptoms. His heart failure and hypertension remained compensated.
problems: Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and with stage 5 chronic kidney disease, or end stage renal disease
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic peripheral angiopathy without gangrene
Acquired absence of left leg below knee
